title: Oct 6 Results + Oct 7 Preview: One Hit, One Miss, Zero Excuses
summary: We went .500 yesterday. Let me be honest—that Braves pick was a disaster.

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest: Yesterday Was Painfully Average

A 1-1 record. Fifty percent accuracy. The definition of mediocrity. Look, I'm not here to sugarcoat it or spin some narrative about how we "learned valuable lessons." We went .500, which means we might as well have flipped a coin.

The Padres pick? Chef's kiss. We nailed that one at 65% confidence and they delivered. But that Braves pick at home against the Dodgers? Absolutely embarrassing. Sometimes the favorite just doesn't show up, and we got burned.

## The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly

**The Good:** The Padres came through like we knew they would. That 65% confidence wasn't just a number—it was a statement. Home field advantage, better pitching matchup, momentum on their side. Everything clicked.

**The Bad:** Betting on the Braves at 50% confidence was basically admitting we had no idea what would happen. And guess what? We were right to be uncertain because they got demolished.

**The Ugly:** Going .500 means our subscribers would've been better off just picking their favorite jersey colors. That's not analysis—that's astrology.

## Tomorrow's Slate: White Sox vs Guardians

Now let's talk about October 7th, and buckle up because this is where it gets spicy. Our model is giving us the Chicago White Sox against the Cleveland Guardians. Yes, you read that right. The WHITE SOX.

Daniel Espino takes the mound for Cleveland while Sean Newcomb goes for Chicago. And here's the controversial part: we're only at 50% confidence. Again.

Let me be brutally honest—a 50% pick is essentially the model shrugging its shoulders and saying "could go either way." But sometimes that's the reality of baseball. It's chaotic, unpredictable, and refuses to follow anyone's script.

## Why The White Sox? (Even If We're Not Super Confident)

Look, I'll be the first to admit this isn't a slam dunk. 50% confidence means this is basically a toss-up. But here's why we're leaning Chicago:

**Sean Newcomb at home** has shown flashes of competence this season. Not brilliance, not dominance, but competence. And sometimes that's enough.

**Daniel Espino** has been wildly inconsistent for Cleveland. When he's on, he's electric. When he's off, he's batting practice.

**Home field at Guaranteed Rate** could be the difference maker in a coin flip game.

But let's not pretend this is anything more than what it is: an educated guess wrapped in statistical analysis. If you're looking for certainty, go watch a rerun where you already know the ending.

## The Bottom Line

Yesterday was forgettable. Tomorrow might be too. But that's baseball—you grind through the mediocre days to get to the hot streaks. We're not going to apologize for a .500 day, and we're not going to oversell a 50% confidence pick.

What we WILL do is keep giving you the honest truth, even when it's uncomfortable. Even when it means admitting our model is basically shrugging.

White Sox tomorrow. Take it or leave it. We'll be back on Oct 8 to either own this pick or roast ourselves for it.

**—Rico**
